“Properties” are stated principally at cost and are depreciated using the group method whereby assets with similar characteristics, use, and expected lives are grouped together in asset classes and depreciated using a composite depreciation rate. This methodology treats each asset class as a pool of resources, not as singular items. We use approximately 75 depreciable asset classes.
Depreciation expense is based on our assumptions concerning expected service lives of our properties as well as the expected net salvage that will be received upon their retirement. In developing these assumptions, we utilize periodic depreciation studies that are performed by an independent outside firm of consulting engineers and approved by the STB. Our depreciation studies are conducted about every three years for equipment and every six years for track assets and other roadway property. The frequency of these studies is consistent with guidelines established by the STB. We adjust our rates based on the results of these studies and implement the changes prospectively. The studies may also indicate that the recorded amount of accumulated depreciation is deficient (or in excess) of the amount indicated by the study. Any such deficiency (or excess) is amortized as a component of depreciation expense over the remaining service lives of the affected class of property, as determined by the study.

message.content: I have sufficient evidence. Let me compute the capex change.

Yes — Norfolk Southern both increased capital investment modestly and completed a major asset acquisition in 2024.

**Capital investment (property additions / capex)**
- Cash paid for property, plant and equipment (`PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment`, USD): **$2,381 million in FY2024** vs. **$2,327 million in FY2023** and **$1,948 million in FY2022** — a ~2.3% year-over-year increase in 2024 (fact IDs 858306, 858300, 858292; 10-K accession 0000702165-25-000008, filed 2025-02-10).
- Total "Property Additions" (which include the CSR acquisition) were **$4,024 million in 2024**, up from $2,349 million in 2023 and $1,948 million in 2022 (2024 10-K, "Railway Property" section, chunk 702165/nsc-20241231:41600). Within that, road/other property rose to $1,711M (from $1,525M) and equipment was $670M (from $802M).
- For 2025, management expects property additions to approximate **$2.2 billion** — a forward-looking plan, not an actual result (chunk 702165/nsc-20241231:147200).

**Major asset acquisition**
- On **March 15, 2024**, Norfolk Southern completed the acquisition of a **337-mile railway line from Cincinnati, Ohio to Chattanooga, Tennessee from the Cincinnati Southern Railway (CSR) for $1.7 billion** (approximately $1,643 million reflected in 2024 property additions). The line had previously been operated under an operating lease, which was terminated at closing (2024 10-K, Note on "Acquisition of Assets of Cincinnati Southern Railway," chunk 702165/nsc-20241231:220800; also chunk 702165/nsc-20241231:36800).
- This acquisition was the main driver of the increase in cash used in investing activities ($2.8B in 2024 vs. $2.2B in 2023) (chunk 702165/nsc-20241231:147200).
